fieldValues.title: Serve dedicated clones, accept a write only where it can reach main on its own, and save it by a tool beside the server
fieldValues.move: The server accepts a write only where that write can reach main on its own; the registry's readOnly flag is the whole policy (owner's choice, 2026-11-04). Every entry points into a dedicated clone that no session works in. A read-only clone only fast-forwards. A writable clone sits on a local branch of main plus unmerged writes, so sessions read their own writes, and a save pass validates, commits, rebases, pushes a per-machine branch and opens a pull request that merges itself on green, reporting pending, behind and held per repository. The server stays out of git. The clerk holds the proof of concept as one self-contained module whose only inputs are the registry and arguments; the rule, layout, steps and status shape are written down so a generic tool can lift them.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: Two sessions updating the same record can still lose a write until a per-repository lock file exists (SP-144). Writes scoped to a feature branch stay with the CLI in a worktree. Hosts other than GitHub.
fieldValues.falsifier: The save pass often holds on conflicts or failed validation, or its pull requests stall for more than an hour.
fieldValues.return_when: Someone outside this workspace wants it, or the status shape and steps go unchanged through two cycles of real use: then extract the generic tool and decide its home.
